items.title: Building material inventory
items.text:
The tool develops its own methodology for quantifying materials in buildings and urban blocks, with results interoperable with the coordinated work of DECUB. The inventory retains the available granularity and is not limited by the exchange format.

Development status

Available: PostgreSQL configuration, migrations for the five schemas: sources, catalog, physical inventory, methodology and results. The catalog and HULC importers are available, with offline validation, simulation, batch writing and versioning. A read-only private explorer with model navigation, construction visualizations and a simplified architectural viewer with an overview and diagnostics by type and related elements is available. Persistent ES/EN/FR labels and individual, multilingual and qualitative hierarchical mapping reviews are available. The scientific engine is pending.

items.title: Processing and persistence
items.text:
PostgreSQL is the primary source. SQL filters and relates inputs; Python will implement scientific logic. Polars will be the preferred tabular engine and DuckDB an analytical complement (e.g. queries on Parquet or Arrow). Algorithms will not be duplicated without justification, and no engine is assumed to be faster for everything. Interoperability will be checked with actual tests, including decimal precision and nulls.

Future caching will be selective, with input fingerprints, methodology and code versions, limits and cleanup. DuckDB will use memory and temporary files in data/cache/; its memory limits do not necessarily cover all process consumption. Values in config/defaults/processing.yaml are indicative and not yet applied automatically. Do not replicate PostgreSQL locally. data/raw, data/cache, data/results are private; detailed results may be persisted in the results tables once the services are implemented. Never publish them in Git or Pages.

The ES/EN/FR editorial label layer resides in separate relational tables with foreign keys to the original entities. Its loader and presentation queries are independent of the scientific engine and mapping fingerprints.

Versioned identification supports multilingual names and qualitative trees independent of physical parts. See mappings and decomposition.

items.title: Batch imports
items.text:
The reference adapter groups source records and resolves reference, material, alias and classification keys using queries bounded to relevant identities. Classifications are resolved by level: each parent must exist before creating its children. For densities, the latest adapter property per material is queried; properties from other sources remain unchanged. Changes are written in batches without changing identity or versioning rules.

Identifiers returned by inserts are correlated with input rows through ordered RETURNING; they are not assumed to be consecutive. Provenance of each relationship and the first occurrence of repeated keys are retained. Integrity checks and a single transaction per import are maintained.

See the catalog import guide for format, identity and use.

Each label table uses the same structure. Its composite primary key prevents more than one label per entity and language. The foreign key restricts deletion of the original entity. source_text preserves the translated original; if it no longer matches the entity, presentation queries return NULL and the viewer retains the original. origin records editorial provenance; note can record ambiguity and limitations. These are neither scientific calculation inputs nor material equivalences. The loader does not overwrite differing labels; later revisions must be resolved explicitly.

items.title: Integrity, conventions and versioning
items.text:
Internal BIGINT identity identifiers; external TEXT codes independent of IDs; English technical snake_case names; TIMESTAMPTZ dates; initially NUMERIC(24,10) quantities; variable JSONB attributes. Lengths in m, areas in m², volumes in m³, mass in kg, density in kg/m³, fractions between zero and one. Tonnes derived from kg. NULL means unknown, not zero.

Foundation migrations implement keys, uniqueness, restricted-delete references, FK indexes and range consistency checks. Revision 0006_integrity strengthens declarative constraints with PostgreSQL functions and triggers for hierarchies, densities, classification domains and mapping selection. Scientific compatibility of methods and profiles still requires application validation. Do not assume a future constraint already exists.

Object Strategy File SHA-256, retain private original Import Adapter and version Classification System and version Property Alternative or successor record Model and assembly Explicit versions Profile and mappings Explicit versions; selected inputs protected when sealed Run Commit, configuration, fingerprint and result references; generation and validation pending

A fingerprint does not replace retaining inputs. Reproducible results require references to exact versions and properties. Do not silently modify used versions. Inventory uses composite FKs to protect consistency of level, identifier and element type, successor model series and nested part version. Partial unique indexes protect order among sibling parts. Complete version immutability, element relationship semantics, units and double counting require later validation. Do not enable partitioning or indiscriminate indexes without measurements.

Methodology enforces uniqueness of versions, roles, assumptions and interpretations within their scopes, fractions between zero and one, explicit basis and JSONB objects. Validation of sums, method compatibility, sufficient assignments and immutability remains pending in Python services.

Results adds composite FKs between run, model, element, assembly, part, mapping set and material assignment; it checks that the referenced property corresponds to the material. Model aggregates have unique grain even with NULL dimensions. Unknown quantities remain NULL; coverage, classification and method version selection and calculation consistency require application validation. See results.

items.title: Classification domains
items.text:
Association Supported classification_systems.domain values Material material, material_category, waste Building building_typology Element component Result material category material_category Result component component

Systems can retain other nonempty domains, but cannot be used in these associations without explicitly extending the contract. System domain, version system, node version, property type code/canonical unit and property type are not editable after creation. New identities or versions will be created when necessary. Descriptive names remain editable; this is not equivalent to freezing a scientific dataset.

items.title: Execution and concurrency
items.text:
Triggers are installed via Alembic, not metadata.create_all(); alembic check does not itself verify functions or triggers. CI runs insertion and rejection tests against isolated PostgreSQL and a downgrade/reapply cycle. Hierarchy checks traverse the entire graph after each relevant statement and serialize writes with SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE. Import in batches and use READ COMMITTED (default); conflicts/deadlocks may require retrying the entire transaction. REPEATABLE READ is rejected for hierarchy writes and mapping selection; SERIALIZABLE requires retry handling. Performance and concurrency have not yet been measured. Hierarchy-writing roles need permission to acquire that lock.

The migration also checks existing rows through logically unchanged updates; an incompatible record aborts migration rather than being corrected or deleted automatically. Downgrade removes only the added constraints and triggers.

items.title: Limits
items.text: Complete version and dependency closure, scientific selection of methods and measurements, dimensional and bulk/intrinsic density compatibility and double-count prevention are still missing. Later revisions incorporate aggregate contributions and selected-input sealing. A FK or trigger alone does not ensure scientific validity.

items.title: Result resolution (0007_resolution)
items.text: The scope constraint distinguishes element, part measurement and component contributions; it retains existing FKs and requires a complete chain where applicable. Partial indexes limit scope duplicates; the trigger checks the component domain. Selection of nonoverlapping scopes and input sufficiency remain pending in the Python engine. Downgrade rejects existing aggregate data. See results.

items.title: Reproducibility (0008_reproducibility)
items.text:
• The manifest is generated in PostgreSQL from an explicit selection; the snapshot is retained and fingerprint computed without converting numeric values to float in Python.
  • Triggers prevent updating or deleting sealed inputs, altering sealed configuration and models or modifying results of finalized runs. They do not prevent new rows in logical sets; complete selection remains the scientific service’s responsibility.
  • Sealing takes SHARE locks on selected tables in stable order and requires READ COMMITTED isolation; input updates and deletions also require that isolation. Result writes lock their run to serialize with sealing/finalization. Keep transactions short and retry transactions aborted by deadlock. Concurrency and performance require representative tests.
  • Downgrade is blocked if manifests, finalized runs or explicit measurements in quantities exist, preventing loss of historical protection.
  • Triggers protect ordinary DML operations, not administrative operations such as disabling triggers or truncating tables. Separate migration/administration role from application role and do not grant TRUNCATE or DDL to the latter.
  • Do not duplicate the entire database: select only relevant inputs. The manifest may contain private source records and remains in the database; never publish it in documentation or repositories.

items.title: Identity, classification and scope
items.text:
erDiagram
    BUILDINGS ||--o{ BUILDING_CLASSIFICATIONS : classified
    BUILDING_MODELS ||--o{ BUILDING_MEASUREMENTS : measured
    ELEMENTS ||--o{ ELEMENT_CLASSIFICATIONS : classified
    CLASSIFICATION_NODES ||--o{ BUILDING_CLASSIFICATIONS : assigns
    CLASSIFICATION_NODES ||--o{ ELEMENT_CLASSIFICATIONS : assigns
    ELEMENTS ||--o{ ELEMENT_RELATIONSHIPS : origin
    ELEMENTS ||--o{ ELEMENT_RELATIONSHIPS : destination
    BUILDING_MODELS ||--o{ PART_MEASUREMENTS : scope
  • Block and building codes are unique within their parent territorial entity. Models are identified by building, code and version. A successor belongs to the same model series.
  • An element’s level and identifier scope must correspond to its model. Namespaces can be added within that model; mappings between different representations are expressed through explicit relationships between elements. Identity is not inferred from similar names.
  • element_kind distinguishes window, opaque and future types. Property tables have a discriminator protected by a composite FK; a specialized row is not mandatory if attributes are missing.
  • Review statuses are draft, reviewed, retired; measurement quality status is independent (unknown, reported, measured, estimated, derived, reviewed). An unknown measurement remains NULL, without a default value.
  • Part positions start at 1 and are unique among siblings, including root parts. Order does not by itself imply exterior/interior orientation. Hierarchies and successions prohibit self-references; revision 0006_integrity also checks longer cycles of parts and models.
  • assignment_type distinguishes reported and reviewed classifications. Classification domain, canonical units and selection of current measurements and assignments require validation in future services. Versions are not yet immutable by SQL constraint.
  • Relationships can represent equivalences between models; physical relationships, e.g. opening-wall, will require scope and semantic checks. Part measurements aggregated by model may exist before elements are assigned to the assembly.

items.title: Synthetic assembly example
items.text: A fictitious façade can have an assembly with several ordered parts, reused by several elements. Thickness belongs to each part; area belongs to element measurements or an aggregate source measurement. The interpreted material will be assigned in the methodological context, not in this table. For windows, frame, glass and air cavity may be represented as parts with different methods.

items.title: Import criteria
items.text:
The HULC adapter distinguishes windows from opaque enclosures according to the original structure, retaining identifier, type, orientation, properties and source row. The component code will be an external classification, not the technical table type. Reported areas are stored as reported_area until it is known whether they are gross or net. A construction name is not a global identity. Layers are imported even without a material mapping. Source subtotals serve to cross-check quantities and are not added to disaggregated results. Zeros derived from missing inputs are not interpreted as confirmed absence.

A future geometric representation may reference elements through model and namespace IDs. Automatic HULC–IFC correspondence or ID stability across exports is not assumed.

Revision 0005_results adds supporting unique keys to element_constructions (id, element_id, construction_version_id) and building_measurements (id, building_model_id) for composite FKs in results.

0006_integrity checks classification domains for buildings (building_typology) and elements (component), and requires nonempty type and unit in all measurements. Dimensional compatibility remains pending. See integrity.

0007_resolution adds supporting uniqueness (id, part_id, building_model_id) in part_measurements, to reference aggregated measurements from results without inventing elements.

Revision 0008_reproducibility adds uniqueness (id, element_id) to element_measurements to reference an effective measurement from an individual contribution. Measurements selected in manifests are protected against ordinary changes; alternatives are recorded as new rows.

items.title: Categorized inventory adapter
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Categorized workbook] --> B[Original records]
    A --> C[Versioned physical model]
    C --> D[Elements and measurements]
    C --> E[Assemblies and parts]
    B --> D
    B --> E

Original category codes are retained in elements.metadata.source_category, without assuming equivalence to catalog classification systems. Only opaque constructions with an exact normalized name match are linked directly. Windows retain their properties without automatic assignment of assemblies or frame or glass geometries. Parts are recorded as source_part until their function is interpreted. Levels, building reference areas and containment relationships are not inferred.

Aggregated measurements for each part remain separate from individual areas. Cached formula volumes with missing inputs are recorded as unknown (NULL); original values remain in sources.source_records. Do not add aggregate measurements and individual quantities without resolving overlaps. A cached volume does not necessarily equal solid material volume. The import report identifies constructions without a physical name match and formulas with missing inputs.

The importer resolves opaque construction names without a direct match through explicit equivalences confirmed by the operator. The association is stored in element_constructions; the original name remains in opaque_properties.construction_name and the source record. Normalized configuration is retained in sources.imports.configuration and forms part of snapshot identity when it contains equivalences. Building identity is not changed and direct matches are not overridden. Windows and part-to-material mappings are outside this operation. See HULC inventory import.

items.title: Batch writing and traceability
items.text:
The importer groups source records, construction versions and parts, elements, measurements, subtypes and associations according to their dependencies. Existing assembly keys and latest versions are queried in groups. Entities generating identifiers request RETURNING with explicit parameter-order correlation; correspondence is not inferred from sequence continuity. Dependent relationships are written after retrieving the corresponding identifiers.

Constraints, triggers and the transactional advisory lock are retained. Unknown data, original names, physical fingerprint and scientific configuration do not change with a different batch size. The entire load is committed together. Simulation still writes no records.

items.title: Interpretation and validation
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Physical part] --> B[Versioned mapping]
    B --> C[Material A]
    B --> D[Material B]
    P[Versioned profile] --> B
    P --> E[Versioned method]
    E --> F[Future quantification]
    C --> F
    D --> F

Version statuses are draft, reviewed and retired. Interpretations distinguish pending, mapped and excluded. A pending interpretation may exist without method or materials. A mapped interpretation requires a method; sufficient assignments will be verified in the validation service. Exclusion requires justification; it does not imply zero quantity.

Fractions may be volumetric (volume), mass-based (mass) or area-based (area). A fraction may be unknown (NULL); a reported value requires an explicit basis. Other methods can use their own parameters without a fraction. The current model supports one assignment per material and interpreted part: contributions of the same material will be consolidated or modeled through distinct parts. A universal fraction sum of one must not be imposed: it depends on the method, voids and scope.

A profile may be in draft without a selected mapping set. The configuration_hash fingerprint has hexadecimal SHA-256 format; computing and verifying the fingerprint, canonical serialization and retaining effective inputs remain pending. The fingerprint alone is insufficient to reproduce a run. Future services will validate role and method compatibility, parameters, assignments, sources, completeness and statuses, as well as immutability of used versions. The database does not yet perform these cross-row checks or execute algorithms.

Revision 0005_results adds supporting unique keys to part_mappings (id, mapping_version_id, construction_part_id) and material_assignments (id, part_mapping_id, material_id) for composite FKs in results.

0006_integrity prevents changing the mapping selection of a profile that already has runs. When a profile fixes a versioned mapping set, the run must respect it. See integrity. Immutability of other parameters and dependencies is not yet guaranteed.

The single-material review service loads new sets/versions, per-part decisions and individual assignments without fractions. Version notes contain the reviewer and input/review fingerprints, and name-to-code resolutions when names are submitted. The service validates this subset of decisions; it does not replace future constraints for composite methods or select profiles.

Persisted totals and indicators are initially limited to a model. Aggregates for buildings with several models, blocks and areas will be calculated in Python, selecting nonoverlapping representations. Each total may refer to a material, a material category or all materials; optionally it is disaggregated by component. Classification nodes already identify a version. Groups at different levels are not additive: do not mix overall totals with breakdowns. Domains are validated in PostgreSQL since 0006_integrity; consistent version selection belongs to the service.

items.title: Cross-schema consistency
items.text:
The revision adds five UNIQUE constraints to existing tables so that composite result FKs can check identifiers and their scopes together. It does not change earlier revisions.

Table Supporting unique key inventory.element_constructions uq_ec_result_scope: id, element_id, construction_version_id inventory.building_measurements uq_bm_result_scope: id, building_model_id methodology.part_mappings uq_pm_result_scope: id, mapping_version_id, construction_part_id methodology.material_assignments uq_ma_result_scope: id, part_mapping_id, material_id catalog.material_properties uq_mp_result_material: id, material_id

The material quantity must belong to the model included in the run. At element resolution, it must belong to the element assembly; the part must belong to the correct assembly version, and the assignment must belong to the mapping of that part and the set selected by the run. The density property, if referenced, must correspond to the same material. Effective density is retained numerically; revision 0006_integrity requires the referenced property to be of type density in kg/m3, with positive finite values. Selection of the effective value and its physical basis belongs to the engine. PostgreSQL requires a fixed profile mapping to match the run mapping; review statuses and scientific method selection will be validated in Python. A valid reference is not assumed to be scientifically appropriate.

items.title: Statuses and unknown quantities
items.text:
Status Volume and mass calculated Both reported estimated Both reported, traceable assumption partial At least one quantity reported; may be known subtotals pending Both NULL excluded Both NULL confirmed_absent Both zero, justified absence

Parts not yet associated with a material will be recorded as issues, not artificial materials. A completed run status indicates that it has finished, not that its inventory is complete. Services must validate justifications, mapping statuses and completeness. Partial quantities must not be confused with complete totals. Aggregate unique indexes treat NULL dimensions as the same absence (using coalesce to 0); generated identifiers are positive.

items.title: Indicators and coverage
items.text:
Initial indicators are nonnegative ratios with a positive denominator from a measurement of the same model. An absent measurement may leave the denominator and indicator NULL. The engine must validate units, measurement type, ratio calculation and denominators; the database does not recalculate formulas. Indicator definitions are versioned so that changes in units or meaning do not replace historical values.

Mass and volume coverage are independent, optional and between zero and one. If coverage is known, its basis is recorded; details can retain numerator, denominator and coverage scope. A universal coverage formula is not yet defined. The engine must check that coverage is interpretable, not estimate it merely from row count. Actual results remain in authorized private storage.

Synthetic example

A contribution with known volume and unknown density has NULL mass and partial status. Another contribution with known mass can be aggregated, but the total must declare that it is partial. Unknown mass is not converted to zero, nor is the percentage of complete contributions interpreted as the percentage of known mass.

items.title: Reproducibility and persistence
items.text:
Each run retains profile, mappings, code version, configuration and SHA-256 fingerprint. Revision 0008_reproducibility adds a selected-input manifest and protects finalized results. The engine must identify all effective dependencies and consume sealed inputs; fingerprint format alone does not guarantee scientific reproducibility. The commit is optional. Writer, aggregator, indicator calculation and automatic retention policy do not yet exist. Detailed persistence is optional.

0006_integrity adds unique keys (id, building_model_id), (id, element_id) and (id, construction_part_id) in material_quantities, and corresponding composite FKs in calculation_issues. If a quantity is reported, every non-null dimension of the issue must match it; an omitted dimension can be derived from the quantity. See integrity.

items.title: Contribution resolution
items.text:
Revision 0007_resolution retains the seven schema tables. No fictitious elements are created to store estimates or aggregate measurements.

flowchart TD
    E[Element and assembly] --> Q[Material contribution]
    P[Part measurement and model] --> Q
    B[Building measurement or source record] --> Q
    Q --> V[Selection of nonoverlapping scopes in Python]
    V --> T[Totals and indicators]
Resolution Additional mandatory references Prohibited references element Element, element-assembly association, version, part and mapping chain Aggregate fields part_measurement Version, part, mapping chain, part measurement, component, coverage key Element, element-assembly association, building measurement component Component, coverage key and at least one building measurement or original record Element, assembly, part, part measurement and mapping chain

Run, model, material and method are mandatory in every case. A component result may come from an external measurement or direct estimate without layer-level mapping; the method and calculation details must explain its interpretation. A reference to an original record alone does not establish that it belongs to the model: the importer or service must check this. Partial quantities can be retained, e.g. mass without volume. Measurements may be pending; sufficiency and units will be validated in Python.

coverage_key identifies a stable physical scope within the model. It must be reused for alternative measurements of the same scope; it is not a file fingerprint or geometry identity. Partial indexes prevent exact duplicates by scope and contribution but do not establish that two different scopes do not overlap. Do not automatically add rows of different resolution: first select a nonoverlapping representation for each physical component. A part result and a component result may be alternatives, not additive quantities. This policy and its manifest still require Python implementation.

Downgrade to 0006_integrity is rejected if aggregated contributions exist, to avoid data loss. Previous rows retain their element resolution.

items.title: Input and result sealing (0008_reproducibility)
items.text:
calculation_runs.input_manifest is a nullable JSONB object until sealing. material_quantities.element_measurement_id (nullable BIGINT) references (id, element_id) in inventory.element_measurements, with FK fk_mq_element_measurement_scope, an index and CHECK requiring element resolution when supplied. An area is not required when the method does not use it.

flowchart LR
    A[Create running run] --> B[Register models]
    B --> C[Select inputs and parameters]
    C --> D[Seal manifest and SHA-256]
    D --> E[Calculate from sealed inputs]
    E --> F[Persist contributions and indicators]
    F --> G[Finalize and freeze results]

The decub.pg-jsonb.v1 manifest contains rows (table, identifier, complete record), parameters, models, profile, mappings, configuration, code version, commit and run type. SHA-256 is calculated over the PostgreSQL JSONB textual representation in UTF-8; interoperable canonical serialization across engines or PostgreSQL versions is not promised. The exact document is retained, not just its fingerprint.

The decub.results.reproducibility.seal_run(connection, run_id, selection, parameters) service requires a caller-controlled transaction and returns the fingerprint. Selection is a map of qualified table names to positive identifiers. The profile, mappings if present and all registered models are required. Synthetic example:

from decub.results.reproducibility import seal_run

# Inside a transaction, after registering the run and its models.
fingerprint = seal_run(connection, run_id, {
    "methodology.profile_versions": [profile_id],
    "methodology.mapping_versions": [mapping_id],
    "inventory.building_models": [model_id],
    # Add all other effective inputs of the method.
}, parameters={})

The example is not a sufficient selection to calculate a real building. PostgreSQL captures records and rejects completion if direct references of quantities, aggregates and indicators are not selected. Transitive dependency closure is not discovered automatically and scientific validity of parameters is not verified. Calculation details must record additional inputs per contribution where appropriate.

A sealed run retains its configuration and models; while running it accepts result writes. Upon finalization (completed, failed, cancelled), run rows and results are protected against ordinary changes. Earlier historical runs without a manifest do not become reproducible retroactively. New runs are created running without a manifest; a provisional 64-character hexadecimal fingerprint is replaced when sealed and is not a scientific fingerprint. Only completed requires a manifest; failures and cancellations before sealing are possible.

Sealing retains and protects selected records, not every row in a logical version. New observations or versions may be added without changing sealed records. The engine must use only the fixed selection, not indiscriminately query new rows of a version. Complete version and dependency closure policy remains pending.

These are neither scientific calculation inputs nor material equivalences. The loader does not overwrite differing labels; later revisions must be resolved explicitly.

items.title: Development and contribution
items.text:
Use short-lived feat/..., fix/..., docs/... branches and pull requests to main. Each change must include relevant tests and update affected current documentation. Do not create pages for every correction. Keep scientific methods, parameters, persistence and visualization separate; avoid material-specific values embedded in algorithms.

python -m pytest
ruff check .
python tools/check_public_tree.py
python tools/build_docs.py

Do not edit applied migrations; create a new revision, review it and test it against isolated PostgreSQL. Do not enable autogeneration for schemas of other applications. Documentation publication uses only docs/es/, docs/en/, docs/fr/ and public resources.

items.title: Versioning and generated artifacts
items.text:
The program follows MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (0.x while the API and methodology evolve). Increment MINOR for functional milestones and PATCH for fixes to a published version; reserve 1.0.0 for a first stable, scientifically validated version. The single source is src/decub/__init__.py; setuptools derives package metadata from it. Update README and CHANGELOG in all three languages when changing the version and reinstall the editable package (python -m pip install -e ".[dev,docs,visualization]"). Check decub --version.

Annotated tags v0.1.0–v0.7.0 are retrospective functional milestones established on 26 November 2026 on commits integrated into main; they do not represent independent package releases or guarantee that historical metadata matches the tag. Do not rewrite commits or move existing tags. Starting with v0.8.0, create annotated tags on the integrated and validated commit, with consistent internal version, metadata and CHANGELOG. Review the commit and publish the tag explicitly; a tag alone is not a distribution or a GitHub Release. Subsequent documentation-only changes do not necessarily require a program version bump.

build/ contains temporary Zensical work (including the single-language destinations standalone-es, standalone-en and standalone-fr) and may contain setuptools artifacts; dist/ contains generated packages and site/ the compiled website. All three directories are excluded from Git. They can be regenerated; first stop any build or preview using them.

items.title: Web publication
items.text:
The main repository may remain private. The sibling public repository decub-material-intensities-calculation-docs (same organization) contains exclusively the compiled website. Do not edit it manually: its main branch is replaced by static files on each publication.

flowchart LR
    A[Markdown in main repository] --> B[Zensical and checks]
    B --> C[Public documentation repository]
    C --> D[GitHub Pages]

Initial configuration by an administrator:

  1. Create the sibling public repository with README and main branch.
  2. In Settings → Pages select Deploy from a branch, main, / (root).
  3. Create a fine-grained access token with access only to the public repository and Contents: Read and write permission. Store it as Actions secret DOCS_PUBLISH_TOKEN in the main repository. Do not store it in files or share it. The organization may require approval.
  4. Review public content and run the Documentation workflow from main. It also runs when changes are integrated into main.

The workflow builds with the organization's public URL, validates file types (including exact path exceptions for Zensical's assets/javascripts/LICENSE and its English and French counterparts) and basic credential patterns, and publishes the static artifact through a separate job. The publishing secret is used only in that job. The main repository history is not copied. Publication requires institutional authorization; automated checks do not replace content review. The local site retains its usual address.

Privacy: do not add actual sources, derived data, geometries, credentials or results to the repository. .gitignore does not remove already tracked files; review git status and the diff before each commit. Examples and tests must be synthetic. The distribution license requires confirmation from the responsible parties.

The Git index check detects restricted paths and some credential patterns; it does not replace content review or detect all potentially sensitive data. Run it after staging changes for commit.

items.title: PostgreSQL integration
items.text:
CI runs a PostgreSQL 14 and 16 matrix with Python 3.12. Each version has its own disposable service and executes the same checks, including migrations, integration tests and the downgrade/reapply cycle. Both jobs must pass before deployment. A failed version does not cancel the other check. The matrix does not use production credentials or connections. Official images follow minor updates for each major version.

Tests in tests/test_postgres_integrity.py are skipped by default. Running them requires an isolated instance with database decub_test, applied migrations and explicit DECUB_TEST_DATABASE_URL configuration. Each test rolls back synthetic records; sequences may advance. CI additionally runs alembic downgrade base and reapplies revisions to its disposable service. Never perform that downgrade against production. Triggers are tested by inserts and updates, not merely by metadata introspection.

items.title: Import performance validation
items.text: Integration tests compare equivalent synthetic imports with batch sizes 1 and 10 on the same isolated database, using a savepoint to undo the first import. They count SQL executions observed by SQLAlchemy/DBAPI; no machine-dependent time threshold is imposed. They also check correspondence between source records and IDs, absence of duplication and rollback following an integrity violation in a later batch. Time improvements over a remote connection must be measured separately.

items.title: Explorer tests
items.text: CI installs the visualization extra together with dev and docs. Offline tests check bounded queries, parameters and relationships, and a Streamlit interface test simulates missing configuration. PostgreSQL integration checks actual queries and rejection of writes in a read-only transaction. The application runs locally; it is not part of the static documentation artifact. Synthetic tests also check strip order and proportions, frame fractions, unknown values and model scoping; integration tests check that alternative areas do not duplicate counts or get summed.

items.title: Trilingual documentation
items.text:
The repository README and CHANGELOG remain at the root in Spanish, with translations in docs/en/ and docs/fr/. Their initial links allow switching between all three versions. Zensical explicitly excludes these repository documents from the web build; index.md remains the homepage.

Spanish sources are in docs/es/, English sources in docs/en/ and French sources in docs/fr/, with matching relative paths. The docs/zensical.es.toml, docs/zensical.en.toml and docs/zensical.fr.toml configurations maintain equivalent navigation and the main repository link. Spanish is the default; English is published under /en/ and French under /fr/. In the combined build, the native header selector uses explicit deployment-root paths to link to the equivalent page in the selected language. A script reinforces the click destination and retains the anchor if its identifier exists on both pages; otherwise, it opens the equivalent page without an anchor. The link also works without JavaScript. The build checks each destination in the final HTML. To recheck the existing site, run python tools/build_docs.py --check-links (with the same --site-url used for the build, if specified). The single-language editing server does not include this processing. The main repository is private: the link does not grant access permissions. All three configurations share project.extra.scope (the Spanish base URL, replaced when building for publication), so theme preferences are independent of language. The public selector does not change the private explorer or CLI language.

Update all three versions in the same change, including dictionaries, diagrams, abbreviations, examples and navigation. Technical names, SQL contracts and commands remain identical. Structural parity checks do not certify translation semantic equivalence on their own; review content before publication.

python tools/check_docs_languages.py
python tools/build_docs.py
python -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site

Strict builds of all three versions generate site/ only after validating each language's artifacts and combining them. For a public URL, use python tools/build_docs.py --site-url https://example.org/docs/ (replace with the authorized URL). The combined preview allows testing the selector and links with the local server. Permanent configurations remain in docs/; the builder creates and removes a temporary configuration at the repository root, with relative source and output paths inside that root, as required by Zensical. Do not run Zensical directly with the configurations in docs/. To edit a single edition, use python tools/build_docs.py --serve-language es (or en or fr); this mode does not serve the combined build of all three languages. CI and publication use the same builder; the publishing job receives only the validated static site. Each configuration declares edit_uri using / separators and its edition path on main, preventing Zensical from deriving an edit URL from a native Windows path.

Mapping tests use synthetic data, verify that proposals do not assign materials, reject stale reviews and inconsistent decisions, and check the scope of linked or measured parts. PostgreSQL integration checks simulation, writing and reading a new version and rejection of repeated versions. Tests also cover multilingual names, ambiguity, stale labels and persistence of the resolved code.

Editorial labels have a composite primary key (entity and language); tests insert synthetic records without requiring a surrogate id.

items.title: Installation and configuration
items.text:
Requirements: Git, Python 3.11–3.13 (preferably 3.12), and authorized PostgreSQL access to apply migrations. Documentation and offline SQL require no server. Target PostgreSQL versions are 14 and 16, checked through a CI matrix; verify that both jobs passed for the revision to be deployed. Other versions require additional validation.

python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"

Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate. Run from the repository root.

items.title: Connection
items.text: Copy .env.example to .env and configure DECUB_DATABASE_URL with the postgresql+psycopg driver. Use TLS options specified by the administrator; encode reserved characters in the username and password. Do not include secrets in terminal arguments, YAML, documentation or commits. The migration role needs permission to create schemas and tables in the authorized database. Use a limited-access role for ordinary operations when available.

items.title: Revision management
items.text:
decub db history
decub db migrate --sql
decub db status

--sql generates DDL from an empty database without connecting. status queries the revision. Before applying, confirm target database, permissions, absence of schema name collisions and backup with the administrator. Alembic uses the decub_alembic_version table in the default schema; verify that it does not belong to another application.

decub db migrate --apply

Administrative operation

This command modifies PostgreSQL. Run only against an authorized database and after reviewing the SQL. Do not execute downgrades in production without an approved recovery procedure.

items.title: Documentation and checks
items.text:
python tools/build_docs.py
python -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site
python -m pytest

Zensical generates the trilingual site from Markdown with docs/zensical.es.toml, docs/zensical.en.toml and docs/zensical.fr.toml. The combined preview is at http://127.0.0.1:8080/, with English under /en/ and French under /fr/. For another port, adjust --site-url when building and the HTTP server port. See development. The local server allows documentation to be consulted without publishing information. Offline tests do not replace validation against an isolated PostgreSQL instance.

items.title: Check the PostgreSQL target
items.text: Before applying migrations, configure the local connection and run decub db inspect. The command uses a read-only transaction and returns target, user, version, search_path, basic privileges, existing objects and detected revision tables. It creates no schemas and modifies no data. Review authorization and possible collisions with other projects; this is not an automatic guarantee of DDL permissions or structural compatibility. Its output contains infrastructure information: do not publish without review.
