items.title: Export Markdown reports to PDF
items.text:
Optionally, open the repository root in Visual Studio Code and install the Markdown PDF extension (yzane.markdown-pdf). The shared .vscode/settings.json configuration uses .vscode/markdown-pdf.css for A4 reports, paginated tables, figures and page numbering. Run Markdown PDF: Export (pdf) from the command palette with the Markdown file active. The PDF is saved next to the Markdown file, including in subdirectories; keep relative images alongside the source. Open the repository as the root folder, not only the report folder. Preserve existing local VS Code preferences when integrating these settings.

For an explicit page break, use <div class="page"></div> in Markdown. Tables preserve whole words where possible; those with up to four data rows are kept together where feasible, while longer tables can continue with repeated headers. The stylesheet attempts to avoid an isolated last row and adjusts spacing without reducing font size. Pagination depends on the print engine: visually inspect pages, especially wide tables, figures and the final page, before distribution. Store reports and their PDFs containing actual data under data/, outside Git and the public website. The stylesheet does not alter data or the Zensical build.

items.title: Multidisciplinary glossary
items.text: Indicative ES/EN/FR equivalents do not replace definitions in each standard or source. Frequent abbreviations have tooltips in the web version.

items.title: Construction
items.text: Term Explanation ES / FR Floor slab Generally horizontal structural element that supports loads and separates levels. Forjado / plancher Ground-bearing slab Element supported on ground or a prepared base; not necessarily equivalent to a foundation. Solera / dallage Enclosure Element that defines spaces. Cerramiento / paroi Façade Vertical external enclosure of a building. Fachada / façade Roof System protecting the top of a building. Cubierta / toiture Party wall Dividing wall between adjacent properties or buildings. Medianera / mur mitoyen Partition Usually non-load-bearing internal division. Tabique / cloison Joinery Frames, leaves and components of doors or windows. Carpintería / menuiserie Infill block Infill unit between joists in certain slabs. Bovedilla / hourdis Construction assembly Configuration of parts and materials that performs a function. Solución constructiva / complexe constructif

items.title: Materials and physics
items.text: Term Explanation Reinforced concrete Concrete with load-bearing reinforcement, usually steel. Mortar Mixture of binder, fine aggregate and water, with possible additives. Insulation Material or system limiting thermal or acoustic transfer. Frame Part of joinery that defines or supports glazing; its projected area does not determine its solid volume. b factor Dimensionless heat-transfer reduction factor associated with boundary conditions; interpret according to the source. Air cavity Air-filled space between parts; not equivalent to solid material. U-value Heat flow per unit area and temperature difference (W/m²K). Solar factor Fraction of incident solar energy passing through glazing, including secondary gains. Air permeability Air passage under defined pressure conditions. Density Mass divided by volume; specify whether bulk or intrinsic.

items.title: Inventory and methodology
items.text: Term Explanation Material stock Material accumulated in a physical system at a given time. Material intensity Material quantity per unit of a reference magnitude. Gross / net area Measurements before or after exclusions defined by the source. GFA / GV Gross floor area / gross volume; check definition and scope. Coverage Part of the inventory universe with sufficient information according to an explicit criterion. Traceability Ability to locate sources, assumptions and transformations. Uncertainty Limitation of knowledge about a magnitude or model. LoW/Eural European waste classification; it does not by itself identify a construction product. Reuse / recycling New use of products / transformation of waste into materials or products, according to the applicable framework.

items.title: Technology
items.text: Term Explanation HULC Herramienta Unificada LIDER-CALENER for building energy assessment. BIM Building information modeling; integrates objects and attributes. IFC Open format and schema for construction information exchange. Digital twin Digital representation linked to a physical entity, with capabilities depending on the system. Parquet Columnar format for tabular data. Cache Regenerable copy of selected information to accelerate operations. Migration Versioned change to database structure.

items.title: Methodological interpretation
items.text: Term Definition Methodological profile Versioned set of decisions, methods and parameters for interpreting and quantifying inventory. Material mapping Association between a construction part and its constituent materials, with provenance and interpretation method. Volume fraction Proportion of constituent volume relative to reference volume. Mass fraction Proportion of constituent mass relative to reference mass. Area fraction Proportion of area relative to a reference area.

items.title: Results
items.text: Term Definition Grain Level of detail represented by a data row. Coverage Known proportion according to an explicit basis; not necessarily a mass proportion. Reference denominator Magnitude by which a quantity is divided to obtain a comparable intensity. Input fingerprint Cryptographic digest of a run's inputs; it does not replace retaining their versions.

items.title: Decomposition and quantities
items.text: Term Definition Terminal node Leaf with no children; may identify a material, void or unknown. Group node Intermediate interpretation level, not an additional quantity. Bulk density Mass per product volume on a basis that may include voids. Effective volume Volume compatible with the property used for quantification. Thermal break Separation of conductive parts using a lower-conductivity constituent. Partial mass Sum of known contributions that does not establish the total.

items.title: Data imports
items.text:
DECUB provides independent adapters for the reference catalog and HULC physical inventory. Both preserve provenance, identity, versions and unknown values. They do not calculate intensities or resolve material mappings.

Guide Contents Reference catalog Format, densities, classifications, aliases and versions HULC inventory Identities, elements, assemblies and equivalences Modes and diagnostics Offline validation, simulation, application, batches and errors 
flowchart LR
    A[Private sources] --> B[Adapters]
    B --> C[(sources)]
    B --> D[(catalog)]
    B --> E[(inventory)]
    D --> F[Future mappings]
    E --> F

Examples are synthetic. Persistence rules and dictionaries are described in the database.

items.title: Localization audit
items.text: decub labels audit inventories deployed domain tables and text columns and summarizes current, missing and stale labels by language. decub labels export --file data/localization/audit.json adds identities, original texts, current labels and distinct values of selected candidate fields. --language fr --missing-only filters editorial entries lacking a current French label; candidates and totals remain unfiltered. The report is not a load document: conflicts and stale labels require review. Element names, levels and other designations may be private; review before sharing. Numerical measurements, scientific notes, credentials and source paths are not exported. Read-only transaction with a consistent snapshot; existing files are not overwritten. Column inventory does not imply that all columns are translatable.

items.title: Extended editorial labels
items.text:
To load a node, use entity: methodology.decomposition_nodes, part_mapping_id (integer), path (text), source_text (reviewed Spanish label) and labels (explicit languages). For elements and levels use entity: inventory.elements or inventory.levels, id (integer), source_text and labels. Use identities from the same database; do not reuse IDs across installations. Format 1, provenance, dry-run and conflict rejection are retained.

Element names matching external identifiers and level names matching their code are not translated. The audit distinguishes these cases and empty names using not_applicable. Nodes retain reviewed ES/EN labels as fallback; current editorial labels take precedence in presentation, and French falls back to Spanish when absent.

The audit includes distinct orientation and the allowlisted metadata.source_category key, not the entire JSON. reviewed_original distinguishes reviewed ES/EN originals counted as current from persisted editorial labels.

items.title: Reference catalog
items.text:
The reference workbook is an independent source, not an executable methodology. The adapter reads the material lists, component codes and typology grid from Hypothèses; the waste hierarchy and density summary from Code Eural and classification; and bibliographic references from Documentation. It does not import building inventories, derived intensity tables or calculation assumptions.

flowchart LR
    A[Workbook] --> B[Normalize and validate]
    B --> C[Compare existing catalog]
    C --> D[Read-only simulation]
    C --> E[Atomic import]
    E --> F[Source records]
    E --> G[Versioned catalog]

Run from the repository root:

decub import catalog --file "data/reference/catalog.xlsx" --validate-only
decub import catalog --file "data/reference/catalog.xlsx" --dry-run
decub import catalog --file "data/reference/catalog.xlsx" --apply

Review warnings, missing materials and conflicts before applying. Application uses a transaction and an adapter-specific advisory lock. Other writers must not modify the same imported namespace concurrently.

items.title: Reimport and identity
items.text:
An identical binary file with identical configuration and a completed import produces no new writes. Material identities are hashes of normalized names within a namespace; the supported format has no stable material codes. Waste codes are not material identifiers. Renaming a file does not change its identity. A modified file may create new provenance even if the normalized data match.

Classification versions include the normalized hierarchy and memberships; changes create a new version while retaining previous assignments. Changes to density or citation notes create properties linked to their predecessor. Properties from other sources are not overwritten. Existing names are retained and confirmed variants are stored as aliases. Missing materials are reported, not deleted or retired. Simultaneous additions and absences block application unless explicitly resolved or confirmed as independent changes.

For a confirmed rename, use a local JSON map from the new label to the established label:

{"Material sintético renombrado": "Material sintético original"}

Pass --aliases data/reference/aliases.json in both simulation and application and keep the map for future imports. Use --allow-identity-changes only after reviewing intentional additions and removals. There is no fuzzy matching or inference of missing hazard markers. Bibliographic entries and density citations are claims from the source, not independently verified references. Densities come from cached numeric cells (kg/m³); nonnumeric densities are rejected and missing values do not mean zero. The adapter supports the observed fixed worksheet layout; format changes require review. Simulation is indicative; application recomputes the comparison inside its transaction.

See modes and diagnostics, catalog persistence and provenance.

items.title: Spanish, English and French labels
items.text:
Original names, codes, aliases and properties remain intact. Migration 0009_localization creates editorial label tables in the catalog, inventory and sources schemas. The explicit loader works with a local JSON file in data/, separate from catalog imports. Review provenance and translations before loading; do not use labels as scientific equivalences or verified legal waste designations.

decub db migrate --apply
decub labels --file data/localization/labels.json --dry-run
decub labels --file data/localization/labels.json --apply

Synthetic format example (the code and original must exist exactly):

{
  "format": 1,
  "origin": "Example editorial review",
  "entries": [
    {"entity": "catalog.materials", "code": "synthetic", "source_text": "Synthetic material", "labels": {"es": "Material sintético", "en": "Synthetic material", "fr": "Matériau synthétique"}}
  ]
}

Nodes also require system_code; codes and original names must match. Assemblies and parts reuse translations of identical text without inferring physical equivalence. Bibliographic references retain their original citation titles; display translations are not new official titles. An optional note records uncertainties. The loader validates the complete input before inserting, reuses identical labels and rejects conflicts; application is transactional and requires write permissions. Dry-run does not modify PostgreSQL. Do not run concurrently with other writers. No workbook reimport is required to add labels. Mapping reviews retain their original fingerprints; scientific candidate search is not automatically expanded. Original free-text values, codes, units and payloads are neither translated nor replaced.

Dry-run uses a read-only PostgreSQL REPEATABLE READ transaction. If a SQL operation fails, the command reports SQLSTATE when available without exposing queries or private parameters. If tables are missing, first check the status of migration 0009_localization.

0011_french_labels extends all seven language constraints. A file containing only fr is accepted; existing ES/EN labels are unchanged. The migration does not generate translations. Downgrading to ES/EN fails if French rows exist, without deleting them.

items.title: HULC inventory import
items.text:
Synthetic example (identity codes defined by the operator):

 decub import hulc --file "data/hulc/example.xlsm" --study-area area-demo --urban-block block-demo --building building-demo --dry-run

The adapter expects worksheets Superficies con categorias and Hoja1 with the categorized-format headers. Each file represents one source building. The default model code is hulc; use --model for another series. Keep identity codes when updating a building; do not infer identities from the filename. Verify the study area, block and building before using --apply. Simulation writes no data; application runs in a transaction. Workbooks and reports are private.

Identical files are detected by SHA-256 and configuration; a new revision with identical normalized physical content retains the previous model and records new provenance. A changed revision creates a new snapshot of the model and its assemblies, preserving history. Earlier versions are not modified. Comparison ignores element order and formatting but preserves part order. Buildings and assemblies with different names are not merged automatically. The adapter assumes that areas, thicknesses and volumes in the assembly sheet are expressed in m², m and m³; confirm this convention for each source. It does not execute macros or recalculate formulas; expressions and cached values are retained separately.

items.title: Construction equivalences
items.text:
When an opaque construction name in the element list does not match any assembly in the workbook, a local JSON file can be supplied using --construction-aliases. Each key identifies the unmatched original name and its value an existing assembly confirmed by the operator. Synthetic example (data/hulc/construction_aliases.json):

{
  "Muro de ejemplo": "Composición de ejemplo"
}

 decub import hulc --file "data/hulc/example.xlsm" --study-area area-demo --urban-block block-demo --building building-demo --construction-aliases "data/hulc/construction_aliases.json" --dry-run

Keys and targets are normalized like workbook names. Unknown keys, nonexistent targets, duplicate keys after normalization and overrides of direct matches are rejected. The report shows applied equivalences, the number of affected elements and unresolved constructions. An equivalence is an explicit operator decision, not a programmatic verification of physical equivalence. Review assemblies and their sources before confirming --apply with the same configuration. Original names, source records and configurations are preserved. Equivalences apply exclusively to opaque enclosures, not windows. A different effective equivalence configuration creates a different model version without changing the building or series identity; repeating an imported configuration does not duplicate the model. Keep actual JSON files in the private data/ directory.

See modes and diagnostics and inventory persistence.

items.title: Import modes and diagnostics
items.text:
The decub import catalog and decub import hulc adapters require exactly one of these modes:

Mode Reads and validates workbook Queries PostgreSQL Persists changes --validate-only Yes No No --dry-run Yes Yes No --apply Yes Yes Yes

Local validation checks the supported format, measurements, identifiers and applicable equivalences. It returns status: validated, database_checked: false and workbook content counts; these are not insertion forecasts. It cannot detect conflicts with stored identities, previous imports, database-dependent constraints or permissions. For the catalog, missing_materials and conflicts are null in this mode because they have not been queried. Construction assumptions still require scientific confirmation.

decub import catalog --file "data/reference/catalog.xlsx" --validate-only
decub import hulc --file "data/hulc/example.xlsm" --study-area area-demo --urban-block block-demo --building building-demo --validate-only

The --dry-run mode requires a connection and executes a read-only transaction. If it recognizes an imported configuration, it returns already_imported; it does not revalidate every constraint of a new insertion. The --apply mode preserves atomicity: all writes, provenance records and the completed-import marker belong to a single transaction. There are no partial batch commits.

flowchart TD
    A[Workbook and local configuration] --> B[Read and normalize]
    B --> C{Mode}
    C -->|validate-only| D[Local report]
    C -->|dry-run| E[Query identities and versions]
    C -->|apply| F[Transaction lock and query]
    E --> G[Simulation report]
    F --> H[Ordered batch inserts]
    H --> I{Constraints and commit}
    I -->|Success| J[Applied report]
    I -->|Error| K[Rollback]

The diagram represents logical dependencies; modes using PostgreSQL check the connection before reading the workbook. Progress messages are sent to stderr and flushed immediately; row ranges identify the batch being processed, not yet committed. Timings are observations of local execution, not scientific measurements. Stdout retains exclusively the JSON report upon successful completion.

Common option Default Use --batch-size 250 Rows per batch, from 1 to 1000. Does not alter model identity or hash. --connect-timeout 15 s libpq connection limit per target, 0 means no explicit limit; overrides the connection setting for this import. --lock-timeout 60 s Wait limit for each lock acquisition, from 0 to 3600 s; 0 disables it. Only in the import transaction. --quiet No Suppresses progress, not errors or the JSON report.

Connection and lock limits are not a total execution limit. Query times may depend on the server, triggers, volume and latency. Errors identify the phase, controlled validation failures or SQLSTATE category without exposing SQL, parameters or arbitrary driver exceptions. If the connection fails during commit, check the import status before retrying: the client cannot guarantee that the server did not commit.

decub import catalog --file "data/reference/catalog.xlsx" --dry-run --connect-timeout 30
decub import hulc --file "data/hulc/example.xlsm" --study-area area-demo --urban-block block-demo --building building-demo --apply --batch-size 250 --lock-timeout 120

Changing batch size does not change the database. Do not reimport an existing model to benchmark performance: the idempotent path skips writes. Use an isolated test database with synthetic data to measure new imports.

items.title: Foundations and scope
items.text:
The reference shared by DECUB participants coordinates results; it does not prescribe a literal implementation. Custom, traceable and interchangeable methods will be developed, with compatible exports and additional analyses.

Development status

Versioned individual and hierarchical identification is available. Selection of quantities, densities and calculation methods is pending. Examples in this section are synthetic.

items.title: Reading guide
items.text:
• Physical inventory
  • Material mappings
  • Hierarchical decomposition
  • Composite materials and products
  • Areas, volumes and geometry
  • Windows and joinery
  • Densities and properties
  • Assumptions and uncertainty
  • Mass calculation
  • Indicators and intensities
  • Coverage and quality
  • Reproducibility and traceability

items.title: Reference catalog import
items.text: See the reference catalog guide.

items.title: Composite materials and products
items.text:
Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

A complex product may contain several materials, intermediate products and voids. The interpretation tree does not modify the original inventory. Groups contribute no quantities in addition to their leaves; identified leaves do not establish completeness.

items.title: Reinforced concrete and slabs
items.text: Separate concrete matrix and reinforcement. In a ribbed slab, distinguish load-bearing parts, infill blocks and possible voids. A separately recorded topping must not be counted again within another part. Do not extrapolate proportions from the illustration.

items.title: Masonry and multilayer products
items.text: Distinguish units, joints and voids according to evidence. If a bulk density already incorporates voids, do not deduct them again. In insulated boards, membranes and joinery, separate only supported constituents; record unknowns instead of inventing adhesives, polymers or thicknesses.

items.title: Choosing resolution
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Physical part] --> B{Sufficient identification}
    B -->|Single product| C[Individual mapping]
    B -->|Several constituents| D[Qualitative tree]
    B -->|Unknown| E[Pending]
    D --> F[Material leaves, voids and unknowns]
    C --> G[Quantification pending]
    F --> G

See hierarchical decomposition, densities and mass calculation.

items.title: Coverage and quality
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Measurement] --> B[Assembly]
    B --> C[Material assignment]
    C --> D[Method + property]
    D --> E[Quantity]
    E --> F[Indicator + denominator]
Status Interpretation Calculated Sufficient inputs for the method Estimated Identified assumption Partial Only part of the quantity is known Pending Insufficient inputs Excluded Explicit scope decision Confirmed absence Physically justified zero

Coverage will be defined using explicit denominators; the known sum will not be confused with the complete inventory. Densities, methods and mappings will retain provenance and alternatives. Quantification methods are not yet implemented and no real values are included.

items.title: Interpreting counts
items.text:
The mapped, pending and excluded states describe identification decisions, not calculation states. A tree with unknown leaves remains pending even if others are identified. A tree with no explicit unknowns does not establish physical completeness. For example, 3 of 4 parts identified is 75% by count, not by mass. Report basis, universe, exclusions and unquantified data separately. Do not calculate mass coverage without a valid denominator.

See mappings and mass calculation.

items.title: Hierarchical decomposition
items.text:
Status: qualitative hierarchical identification is available; quantities are pending.

Revision 0010_decomposition supports interpreting a terminal physical part through a versioned component tree. inventory.construction_parts is unchanged. Format 1 remains supported; format 2 adds components to every entry (null for individual decisions). To migrate an existing proposal, preserve metadata and fingerprints, change format to 2 and add components: null to each part before editing decompositions.

decub mapping propose --model-id 1 --hierarchical --file data/mapping/review_tree.json

A decomposed entry uses status: "decomposed", material_code: null, a justification and a list of at least two components. Each node has kind, label_es, label_en, justification, material_code and children. Groups require children; leaves cannot have children. Only material leaves accept an unambiguous catalog code or name. Synthetic component example (codes must exist in the review catalog):

[
  {"kind":"material","label_es":"Componente A","label_en":"Component A","justification":"Synthetic evidence","material_code":"synthetic_a","children":[]},
  {"kind":"unknown","label_es":"Componente pendiente","label_en":"Unresolved component","justification":"Synthetic uncertainty","material_code":null,"children":[]}
]
Kind Interpretation group Intermediate grouping without its own assignment. material Reviewed identification of a leaf. void Non-material void in the chosen scope; requires justification. unknown Unresolved component or interpretation; not zero.

The CLI validates scope, original metadata, fingerprint, languages, unambiguous names, justifications and structure (maximum 32 levels and 1,000 nodes per part). A physical parent or retired version cannot be decomposed. A decomposed part remains pending if it contains unknown leaves and becomes mapped otherwise; this does not certify physical completeness, fractions or masses. Simulation returns decomposed, decomposition_nodes and resolved_components (by part and path). Apply using the same review command, only after approval. A catalog assignment is reused if the same material appears in multiple leaves; the tree retains each location. Groups are not additional material contributions.

No child fractions or thicknesses are inferred. The future engine must select a non-overlapping resolution, quantify terminal contributions only, document voids and unknowns, validate conservation of quantities, and seal the effective tree and parameters. Result integration, reuse across models and quantitative estimates remain pending.

See composite products for interpreting trees.

The graphical viewer details represent reviewed trees using illustrative templates. They do not introduce subcomponent measurements or change the inventory.

Editorial localization of each node is stored separately through 0012_extended_labels; see the relational model. It does not change the scientific review format or content.

items.title: Densities and properties
items.text: Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

items.title: Physical basis and selection
items.text:
Property Interpretation Intrinsic density Mass per solid material volume as defined by the source. Bulk density Mass per product reference volume, which may include pores or voids. Areal mass Mass per product area; useful for sheets when documented. Linear mass Mass per length of profile or unit.

Density must match the volume basis of the measurement. Identifying concrete, wood or polymer is insufficient to choose an effective value. Distinguish foamed products, hollow units and solid materials; check moisture and measurement conditions when relevant. Do not treat a generic density as a specific measurement.

items.title: Adding catalog information
items.text:
Retain source, unit, property type, applicability, version and evidence. Distinguish a new material identity from an additional property of a cataloged product. A category without an unambiguous equivalent remains pending; do not substitute another merely because density is available. The catalog supports properties and provenance; effective selection is not yet implemented. See catalog and estimates.

The detail viewer displays current catalog density candidates with their provenance. It does not select effective densities. Reinforcement content, expressed for example in kg of steel per m³ of composite, is a separate property from steel density.

items.title: Areas, volumes and geometry
items.text:
Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

For a homogeneous layer: V = A × e and m = V × ρ, with area in m², thickness in m, volume in m³ and density in kg/m³. Synthetic example: 10 m² × 0.10 m = 1 m³; with a fictitious density of 1,500 kg/m³, the result is 1,500 kg. This example is not a material reference value.

Composite layers, cavities and frames require distinct methods. The frame area fraction is insufficient to obtain its volume. Gross and net areas must not be mixed, nor openings deducted twice. Unmodeled information must be declared out of scope or pending, as appropriate.

items.title: Selection and overlaps
items.text:
Input Proposed rule Gross area Deduct openings only when included and known. Net area Do not repeat the deduction. Thickness Verify unit, physical meaning and representativeness. Aggregate measurement Do not add it to elements it already covers. Voids Distinguish envelope volume from effective volume according to density basis. Unknown Keep pending, with no default zero.

Original measurements are retained; a derived quantity must state formula, inputs and scope. See windows and coverage.

items.title: Indicators and intensities
items.text:
Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

MI = mass / denominator. It can be expressed in kg/m² of reference area or kg/m³ of reference volume. Coordinated results may be disaggregated by material, material category, component and typology. Denominator definition, scope and profile will be retained; element areas are not equivalent to floor area.

items.title: Comparability
items.text:
A synthetic indicator of 2,000 kg / 100 m² of reference floor area equals 20 kg/m². Do not compare it with an envelope-area indicator or different scope without stating differences. If the denominator is missing or invalid, do not produce a fictitious ratio. Partial results must be identified as such.

See coverage and results.

items.title: Physical inventory
items.text:
Status: physical import and versioning are available; measurement selection for calculation is pending.

A model contains elements and their measurements. A construction assembly describes a reusable solution; its parts are not copies of each element. Aggregate part measurements may coexist with individual measurements.

items.title: Interpretation rules
items.text:
• Retain original areas, thicknesses, units and provenance.
  • Distinguish net and gross area, orientations, unmodeled elements and missing data.
  • Do not add individual element quantities to an aggregate that already includes them.

See HULC inventory, physical model and geometry.

items.title: Material mappings
items.text: Status: service available. Identifying a family or product does not approve its density or quantity.

items.title: Profiles and mappings
items.text:
The methodological structure allows versioned methods, profiles, assumptions and mapping sets independent of physical assemblies to be recorded. Selection of alternative sources and parameters is described in the profile, but physical values remain in the catalog. A profile is not yet executable: the Python method registry, source resolution and parameter validation remain missing.

Synthetic example: a part of 1 m³ may contain 0.7 m³ of material A and 0.2 m³ of material B, leaving 0.1 m³ of voids. The volume fraction is not a mass fraction. Coverage must declare voids and unknown quantities without converting them into fictitious materials.

items.title: Single-material mapping review
items.text:
The procedure uses assemblies with non-retired associations or part measurements in the selected model, including those not linked to elements. The review unit is the versioned construction part, not the text description or each element. The catalog material code and name, part ID and source record when available are retained. The catalog is not modified.

flowchart LR
    A[Inventory and catalog] --> B[Private proposals]
    B --> C[Explicit review]
    C --> D[Read-only simulation]
    D --> E[New version]
    E --> F[Identification viewer]

Obtain the model ID in the explorer (inventory.building_models table). Synthetic example: replace 1 with the actual ID. Save the file exclusively under data/ (excluded from Git). Export does not overwrite an existing file.

decub mapping propose --model-id 1 --file data/mapping/review.json

Complete mapping_set (set code), version (new version) and reviewer (responsible person). In each parts entry, modify only status, material_code and justification. The catalog and candidates are included for review. Do not alter metadata or fingerprints.

Status Material Justification pending null Optional: uncertainty or information needed mapped Exact code or unambiguous non-retired catalog name Required: evidence for single-material identification excluded null Required: explicit reason for exclusion

The material_code field also accepts the full original name, a registered alias or a current ES/EN/FR label from catalog.material_labels. Exact codes take precedence; other inputs are compared ignoring case, accents and whitespace while retaining punctuation and word order. Zero or multiple matches reject the review; there is no partial matching or automatic selection. Editorial labels do not change the template fingerprint or original suggestions. When names are used, simulation returns resolved_names with part identifiers and resolved codes. Check that list and, to fix the selection unambiguously before applying, replace names with codes. Application resolves inputs again with current labels locked and records the submitted name and resolved code in the version notes.

Suggestions are normalized name/alias matches and bilingual search terms; even a unique candidate requires review. They are neither equivalences nor probabilities. Reviewers must leave composite parts pending when single-material identification cannot be justified. Parent parts and retired assemblies cannot receive single-material assignments in this procedure. No proportions are inferred: fraction fields remain null. Exclusions do not represent zero mass. Cavities, composite joinery and multi-component assignments require subsequent methodology.

decub mapping review --file data/mapping/review.json --dry-run
decub mapping review --file data/mapping/review.json --apply

Simulation checks content, scope, inventory and catalog fingerprint and version availability. It does not write. Explicit application uses one transaction, temporarily locks input tables and serializes mapping writes; it requires permissions and should run outside concurrent imports. If inputs change, export a new template and review again. If the version exists, use a new one: reviews are not overwritten through this CLI. Retain the private file; the reviewer and SHA-256 fingerprints of inputs and review are recorded. reviewed means explicit review of the decision set, not a complete inventory or certification of catalog materials or densities. The single-material format requires no additional migration once the current schema is installed.

Single-material identification is recorded with method explicit_single_material_identification, domain mapping, version 1. It is not a quantity algorithm. No densities, effective fractions or calculation methods are selected, and no results are created. Universal immutability against direct SQL writes and transitive closure of the future calculation manifest remain pending.

For complex products see hierarchical decomposition.

items.title: Mass calculation
items.text: Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

items.title: Non-overlapping contributions
items.text:
For effective volume V and compatible density ρ, m = V × ρ. Alternatively, documented areal or linear mass can be multiplied by area or length. Do not sum parent and children when they represent the same matter.

Fraction Basis Volume Constituent volume divided by reference volume. Mass Constituent mass divided by reference mass. Area Constituent area divided by reference area.

They are not interchangeable. Check bases, units and conservation within each group. An unknown remainder is not allocated automatically. Sum only compatible, terminal and non-overlapping contributions; if any are missing, the result is partial.

items.title: Synthetic example
items.text:
For 1 m³ of a fictitious composite with 0.8 m³ of A, 0.1 m³ of B and 0.1 m³ of confirmed void, fictitious densities of 1,000 and 2,000 kg/m³ give 800 and 200 kg. Total: 1,000 kg of solids. Do not use these values as actual properties.

See densities, geometry and results.

items.title: Reproducibility and traceability
items.text:
The results schema already supports run and contribution quantities, model aggregates and ratio indicators with their reference measurement. The Python engine is not yet implemented. Mass and volume coverage will be recorded separately and their basis must be justified. Parts without identified materials may generate issues without creating fictitious materials.

Results may use aggregated measurements or component estimates when individual elements do not exist. Selection of nonoverlapping scopes, unit compatibility and documentation of effective inputs must be part of reproducible calculation.

The run manifest fixes effective inputs before calculation. The future engine must select the methods, parameters, assumptions, mappings, measurements, densities and classifications actually used, along with their dependencies, and consume that selection. Sealing does not decide which density or measurement is scientifically appropriate or resolve overlaps.

items.title: Evidence chain
items.text:
Retain original source, normalized measurement, versioned interpretation, effective property selection and results separately. The available sealed manifest protects selected inputs; it does not replace scientific decisions or future transitive closure of decomposition trees. Actual data and reviews are private; documentation uses synthetic examples.

See integrity and assumptions.

items.title: Assumptions and uncertainty
items.text: Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

items.title: Evidence and assumptions
items.text:
• Prioritize specific measurements and verifiable product documentation; assess relevance before use.
  • If direct information is absent, consider justified technical references or scenarios and record applicability.
  • Distinguish estimated, measured, normalized and derived values. Do not invent fractions or assume identical assemblies from shared names.
  • Record reviewer, source, date or version, method, parameters, limits and alternatives; retain previous decisions.

items.title: Uncertainty example
items.text:
Two possible pane thicknesses produce two different scenarios, not an average measurement. Only justified bounds may be reported as an interval; no probability distribution is assumed. If information is insufficient for estimation, leave pending. Exclusion requires an explicit scope criterion.

See coverage and traceability.

items.title: Windows and joinery
items.text: Status: proposed quantification methodology; not yet executed by a scientific engine.

items.title: Area allocation
items.text:
If total projected area A and frame area fraction f use the same basis, A_frame = A × f and A_glazing = A × (1 − f). The fraction must be between 0 and 1 (convert percentages explicitly). Apply per window and sum; do not use a simple average of percentages for different areas. If the area already represents glazing, do not deduct the frame again.

Synthetic example Value Total area 2 m² Frame fraction 0.20 Projected frame area 0.40 m² Glazed area 1.60 m²

items.title: Glass and cavity
items.text: Glass volume is A_glazing × sum of pane thicknesses assuming equal area for all panes. With two fictitious 4 mm panes, the result is 0.0128 m³. Confirm whether the source thickness is per pane or total. Do not include the cavity in solid thickness; it may be explicitly excluded from the solid inventory while retaining its physical presence. Spacers and sealants require their own evidence and geometry.

items.title: Frame and profiles
items.text: Projected area does not determine aluminium volume. When supported, use effective material cross-section times length, linear mass times length, or representative mass per unit. Distinguish hollow profiles, thermal breaks, gaskets and hardware; do not assume their composition. If inputs are missing, leave the contribution pending. See geometry and composite products.

items.title: References and related projects
items.text:
References guide the design; they are not dependencies or sources of automatically adopted values. Private coordination files are not redistributed. Check license conditions for each version and dataset before incorporating code, data or figures.

items.title: Technologies
items.text: PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Polars, DuckDB and Polars, DuckDB limits, Zensical (documentation generator, MIT license). Check the license and version of each installed package.

items.title: DECUB private explorer
items.text: The explorer lets users consult the catalog, physical inventory and provenance in PostgreSQL through a local Streamlit interface. It neither modifies data nor calculates intensities. Public documentation contains synthetic examples only.

items.title: Installation and execution
items.text:
From the repository root, with the virtual environment active:

python -m pip install -e ".[visualization]"
python -m streamlit run src/decub/visualization/explorer.py --server.address 127.0.0.1 --server.port 8501 --browser.gatherUsageStats false

Open http://127.0.0.1:8501. Local PostgreSQL configuration and authorized access are required. Stop with Ctrl+C. Do not expose the port to other networks or deploy to public services. Prefer a PostgreSQL role with SELECT-only privileges; the application starts read-only transactions, which do not replace server-side permission controls. Multi-user authentication is not implemented. Do not publish screenshots, values or downloads of actual data.

items.title: Navigation
items.text:
Section Queries Home Entity counts, including historical versions Architectural viewer Group cards, textured drawings, schematic windows and model diagnostics Building browser Territorial and model selection, breakdowns, records and proportional schematics Materials Identities, properties, aliases and classifications Classifications Systems, versions, nodes and parent references Buildings and models Study areas, blocks, buildings, models and measurements Elements Identifiers, measurements, subtypes and associations Assemblies Versions, parts and aggregated measurements Sources References, files and record locations Imports Adapter, status, dates and statistics Quality Missing scalar density, unmatched opaque elements and part measurements without values Language coverage Label coverage by entity and language

In the table sections, select an entity, filter by identifier, search for literal text and paginate (up to 100 rows per page). Select a record to consult its direct relationships (up to 100 records per relationship); to continue navigating, use foreign key identifiers in the corresponding entities. Parts of an assembly version can be consulted by its identifier, retaining position and parent. An effective scientific version is not selected automatically. Quality counts include historical versions; they do not represent mass coverage or scientific validation. Nulls are not converted to zeros. Decimal values are displayed as text to preserve precision.

flowchart LR
    A[Local Streamlit] --> B[Bounded SQLAlchemy queries]
    B --> C[(PostgreSQL: read-only transaction)]
    C --> A

Queries have a statement timeout and pagination. Original payloads, import configuration and storage paths are omitted; identifiers allow provenance to be followed. There is no persistent data cache. The interface includes no exporters; the browser may allow visible data to be copied. The browser and tables share the same data and read-only transactions. The 3D viewer, certified physical sections and mass and intensity charts remain for later phases.

items.title: Building browser and visualizations
items.text:
In the sidebar, select Navegador de edificios (building browser). Choose a study area, block, building and model version; each selector supports search and pagination. Views work exclusively with the selected version, not with the sum of historical models.

View Visualization and navigation Breakdown Count, recorded area and coverage by element kind, original type, original category, orientation or original opaque construction Elements Filter by the same groups, search and select an element; consult identifiers, measurements, thermal properties, associations and their assembly versions Assemblies Choose a version linked to elements or with part measurements for the model, including assemblies without element associations

The area breakdown includes only elements with exactly one measurement of type area, unit m2, a known value and a quality other than unknown. If alternatives exist, the element is excluded from the area total but not from the count. The number of elements with and without usable area is reported for each group. Groups without values retain a null area; charts omit those values. The sum of recorded areas is not the usable, gross or net building area: it does not resolve overlap between elements or allow individual and aggregate measurements to be added together. Opaque association coverage counts elements with at least one non-retired association; it does not certify equivalences or mass availability. The original construction view includes opaque elements only. Original categories are not scientific catalog classifications. If there are more than 100 groups, partial totals or charts are not presented as complete.

items.title: Assembly schematics and windows
items.text:
The schematic section uses strips whose widths are proportional to the original thickness in millimetres, in position order. It is drawn only if all parts of the version are available (at most 100), flat, have unique positions and positive, finite thicknesses. No material-specific textures or colours are assigned: colours distinguish positions. The thickness sum is arithmetic, not a certification of physical thickness; parts imported as source_part may represent components other than layers in series. If the list is hierarchical, incomplete or has unknown thicknesses, the table is retained without drawing a fictitious section.

Part measurements are filtered by model and assembly version. Areas (m2) and volumes (m3) are displayed separately, without accumulating parts, combining units, selecting alternatives or allocating aggregate data to individual elements. Charts are limited to a complete list of at most 100 records; tables support pagination. A known zero value is not equivalent to missing data.

For a window with a known frame fraction between 0 and 1, a proportional bar shows the frame and remainder (glass under the frame/glass assumption). No dimensions, geometry, thickness or composition are inferred. Thermal properties remain recorded data. Charts use approximate numbers for display; tables preserve source decimals.

items.title: Architectural viewer
items.text:
In the sidebar, open Visor constructivo (architectural viewer) and select a building and model version. The simplified view retains the scientific browser and uses the same read-only queries. Cards are paginated six at a time and show counts and usable individual area with coverage; models and alternative measurements are not combined.

View Grouping criterion Opaque elements Original construction name and version of the sole non-retired association; missing or multiple associations appear as unresolved groups without choosing an assembly Windows Recorded opening name and frame fraction; this is not a geometric or material classification

Assemblies with a complete flat list of positive, finite thicknesses are drawn in oblique perspective, with proportional widths and symbolic height and depth. Numbers identify original positions. Without a selected mapping version, colours and hatches are illustrative and selected from recognizable words in the source description. When a unique recognizable family is unavailable, a neutral texture is used. Serial layers, interior/exterior orientation, material identity, density and mass are not certified. Incomplete or hierarchical lists retain their descriptions without a proportional drawing.

Windows are represented by a normalized square with a uniform border. For frame fraction f, the side of the remaining area is the square root of 1 − f. This preserves the area proportion, not actual dimensions or physical profile thickness. The frame has a neutral appearance, without assuming aluminium or another material. The remainder is interpreted as glass only under the frame/glass assumption. If the fraction is missing, no fictitious window is drawn.

Count and area charts in the scientific browser use ranked horizontal bars, value labels and a consistent palette. Drawings use a neutral paper background legible in both themes; the drawing palette does not adapt dynamically. Figures are local, static and require no external graphical resources. For assemblies without associated elements, aggregate measurements and traceability, use the scientific browser. None of these representations calculates material quantities.

items.title: Building diagnostics
items.text:
The viewer opens Resumen general (overview) by default, with element counts, individual area coverage, distribution, quantification status and model diagnostics. Navigation separates the overview, opaque elements, windows, material inventory and building diagnostics. Open Diagnóstico del edificio (building diagnostics) to filter by severity and issue type and select a record. The rule summary is visible without expanding controls: it includes severity, record counts, distinct related elements and an explanation of the consequence. Cards display their status, counts by severity and type, and allow opening filtered diagnostics. The Ver diagnóstico de todo el modelo (view diagnostics for the whole model) button clears the card filter. Diagnostics are read-only and obtained from current records; they do not store results or change review status.

Severity Interpretation Error Data unusable for the specific check; does not prove that all quantification routes are infeasible Warning Absence, alternative, association or risk requiring review Observation Recorded characteristic or representation limitation that does not necessarily constitute a defect Scope Available rules Elements Missing, alternative, unusable or zero area; missing opaque or window properties; missing or out-of-range frame fraction Associations Opaque elements without a non-retired association or with several; draft associations and linked retired versions Assemblies and parts Assembly without parts; unknown or zero thickness; nested parts; parts without measurements for the model Part measurements Missing value/unknown quality; unexpected area or volume unit; alternatives of the same type Coverage Coexistence of individual area and part area/volume measurements for a version; measured assembly without linked elements

Each issue corresponds to a rule and an identified entity. An entity can have several issues. Rule occurrence counts are distinguished from distinct related element counts: for direct issues, count the element itself; for shared issues, count the elements linked to the version by non-retired associations in the selected model. A card filter restricts the latter count to its own elements. An unlinked assembly may have issues and zero related elements. Do not sum elements across rules or interpret this count as mass coverage. Part and assembly diagnostics include versions linked through non-retired associations or measured in the model. Measurements from other models never fill gaps in the selected model. Coexisting resolutions indicate a risk requiring methodological resolution, not proven physical overlap. Multiple associations may represent legitimate components. A known zero remains distinct from a missing value.

Cards include direct issues for their elements and, for a unique assembly, shared issues for its version and parts. A shared issue may appear on several cards; card counts must not be summed to obtain the model summary. Unlinked assemblies and issues not attributable to a specific card can be viewed in global diagnostics. Records show original data, identifiers and measurements; for a shared issue, elements associated with the version within the model can be paginated, without claiming that all are affected in the same way. The issue list is paginated in groups of 100; counts are not limited to the page.

Effective mappings for a calculation profile, effective density, mass coverage and compliance with a calculation methodology are not yet checked. Future quantification must share a single scientific engine, with explicit profiles and methods, traceable contributions and calculation diagnostics. Until it exists, Inventario de materiales (material inventory) shows pending mass and volume and unevaluated coverage; the overview and cards also indicate pending mass without displaying fictitious zero values. Individual area coverage in the overview is not mass coverage. Absence of issues under the current rules does not certify the scientific validity of the inventory.

items.title: Reviewed identifications
items.text:
The viewer mapping version selector is explicit and defaults to no selection. With a reviewed version, opaque cards show catalog names for supported single-material identifications and catalog-identity textures; remaining parts are neutral. Textures remain representative and do not certify physical properties. Windows retain their normalized diagram without assigning frame material from appearance.

The material inventory displays per-part states and justifications and distinct identification counts, not quantities. Diagnostics distinguish identified, pending, excluded, missing-decision and unsupported-assignment parts. Related elements are distinct per state and non-retired association; counts must not be summed across states. Measured assemblies without elements may have zero related elements. Cards display pending and excluded parts in the visible part list. The 22 physical inventory diagnostic rules remain independent. See the review procedure.

items.title: Multilingual labels
items.text:
The sidebar Idioma / Language / Langue selector controls the entire explorer for the session (ES by default, EN and FR). Navigation, controls, diagnostics, headers and charts are localized through visualization/i18n.py and i18n_messages.py. Entities use current PostgreSQL editorial labels, falling back to the original when absent. Codes, identifiers, justifications and original values are not rewritten. Domain values are translated by context for presentation; source categories without documented correspondence and uninterpreted orientation codes remain codes. Decimal formatting uses commas in ES/FR and points in EN, without rounding Decimal values in tables. Navigation labels are not scientific criteria. Selector options are explicitly decoded from visible text to their internal identity. Changing language keeps the active section and preserves each list selection if it remains available; if it disappears, the first available option is selected. Identical labels are disambiguated using their identifier. Navigation and filter selections may persist during the session.

The Language coverage section shows applicable totals, current, missing, stale, not-applicable and reviewed-original labels by entity and language. If there is no denominator, the percentage is null, not 0 or 100%. It uses the existing read-only audit within a repeatable snapshot; it does not export or modify data. Coverage does not imply specialist linguistic validation, translation of original texts or scientific coverage.

items.title: Component breakdown
items.text:
Select a reviewed mapping version. In opaque cards, open Breakdown for a composite part or Detail for an individual identification. The material inventory allows selecting an assembly and part, including those without linked elements. Window cards display explicitly linked assemblies, with the number of elements in each link. Joinery assemblies with a breakdown but no individual link are displayed separately, without attributing them to windows. Identifications and labels follow the selected version and language.

Details reuse drawing templates for reinforced and fibre-reinforced concrete, ribbed slabs, brick masonry, thermally broken profiles, boards and membranes. Products without a template have a symbolic component representation; individual identifications display a texture sample. Tree paths connect drawing markers and the key. A template is chosen from source descriptions and node labels for graphical purposes only; material textures use reviewed identities. Unresolved components and unconfirmed geometries are neutral. The graphical key includes up to twelve nodes; the textual tree retains all components and justifications. No topping is added to the ribbed slab schematic.

Data Representation Positive original thickness The recorded part value is shown, not a validated thickness of its children. Unknown thickness Synthetic example dimension if a template is available; otherwise a symbolic representation without a measurement. Internal geometry Illustrative, not to scale, without approved fractions. Catalog density Candidates by material code, property identifier, value or range, status and provenance references; up to eight per material, without automatic selection. Effective density or reinforcement content Pending methodological selection; not inferred from drawn shapes.

The synthetic dimension is for illustration only and is not a normative standard value. Unknown quantities are not imputed, and drawing parameters are not stored in PostgreSQL. Steel density (mass per volume of steel) does not determine reinforcement content (mass of steel per volume of the composite) or geometric distribution. Future quantification must provide justified dimensions and fractions for each subcomponent, distinguishing effective density from drawing parameters. Current details do not calculate masses or certify product configuration.

items.title: Texture gallery and graphical conventions
items.text:
In Texture gallery, browse pages of 24 records and search by code, original or current translation. The gallery uses the global selector. Codes, status and identity-bound textures are shown; absent or stale labels fall back to the original. The gallery is read-only.

The visualization/material_textures.py module centralizes immutable vector hatch/color recipes and explicit bindings by stable catalog code. The library reuses the reference adapter’s code-generation function; changing a translation, language or PostgreSQL numeric identifier does not change the texture. Proportional sections, details and keys reuse the same recipes. Before selecting a review, lexical illustration remains provisional and does not identify materials.

The following sheets show the generic graphical vocabulary, not a list of materials present in a building or an export of the private catalog. Patterns are symbolic: graphical density, dots, circles, lines and colors do not encode porosity, fractions, geometry, physical density or actual color. Construction templates provide shape differences (for example, blocks versus a concrete matrix) without changing material identity.

items.title: Representation states
items.text:
State Interpretation Identification pending No usable identity; also applies to retired materials in reviewed views. No specific texture An identity exists, but no unambiguous graphical convention or explicit binding is available. Void Explicitly defined void node; neither a material assignment nor a zero-mass imputation. Exclusion Justified exclusion decision; does not remove the part from the physical inventory. Group Organizational node without its own material assignment.

To extend the library, add or reuse a recipe with ES/EN/FR labels and explicitly bind the stable code in CODE_TEXTURES. New unbound codes retain the generic material-without-specific-texture hatch; an identity is not inferred from similar names. Commercial or ambiguous names do not require inventing their appearance or composition. New materials and densities are managed separately through scientific procedures.

To regenerate the generic sheets after changing recipes, with the visualization extra installed:

python tools/build_texture_gallery.py
python tools/check_docs_languages.py

The generator does not query PostgreSQL or source files. Do not publish screenshots of the private gallery or real buildings.

items.title: Extended editorial labels
items.text: Element names matching external identifiers and level names matching their code are not translated. The audit distinguishes these cases and empty names using not_applicable. Nodes retain reviewed ES/EN labels as fallback; current editorial labels take precedence in presentation, and French falls back to Spanish when absent.
